about_the_game:
Unguided is a roguelite slasher with stamina-based combat drawing inspiration from Tron and 1980s sci-fi artwork and music. The game puts you in control of an inmate in a digital prison with only one way out - get to the remote server of the abandoned human cloning laboratory, upload yourself back into the blank body, and get revenge on the ones who framed you.

  • Master fast-paced, challenging combat that requires precise timing and stamina management. Slash, shoot, and dodge your way through the PIT prison for a chance to live again.

  • Combine attack and defence routines and execute cross-weapon combos to get the most out of your 1N-M8 stack

  • Forge your personal codebase bit by bit, upgrade your 1N-M8 stack, and unlock permanent upgrades to change the way you fight and reach new areas of the PIT

  • Get to the end of the ever-changing system, filled with humanity's most dangerous and twisted minds. Befriend the worst of them. Use raw Source Code to recover your memories or help other inmates rewrite theirs.

"Welcome to the PIT, the most humane prison in the history of mankind. It's a one-way ticket designed with a simple goal in mind - keep the moralists at bay. You see, in 2037, we're executing criminals by the thousands, and apparently, that had upset a religion or two. But what if we could still permanently remove these elements from society, but you know... with all the "thou shalt not kill" part still intact? Enter the Personality Improvement Technology, once a long-buried human mind digitalization program, and a savior to society nowadays. Problem solved - the "immortal" part gets sent to the PIT, and the body gets the good 'ol "...have mercy on your soul" treatment." - from the book "How it's done: Albert Kramer's story"

content_descriptors.notes: Players control an inmate, trying to escape a digital prison. From an isometric perspective, players explore environments based on other inmates' minds. Players engage in melee-style combat against digitalized humans and abstract, primitive-shaped sentinels of the system. Players use digital routines depicted as weapons (swords, spears, revolvers) to kill enemies. Enemies emit pieces of code when injured/killed, with no depiction of realistic blood.
